newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary wheat, maize futures keep rising.
newsitem.headline: Hungary wheat, maize futures keep rising.

text.p: Wheat and maize futures on Hungary's Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued the past three weeks' rising trend on Wednesday in slow trading.
The rise was fuelled by firming world market wheat prices and unconfirmed news on Serb and Croatian interest in buying Hungarian grain, traders said.
"The price of wheat on the international markets increased by some $15 in the past one month, and the Hungarian bourse reacted to that," said Termin Broker's Robert Vajo.
Milling and feed wheat futures rose 400 to 450 forints per tonne on Wednesday. May milling wheat closed at 24,700 forints, while July firmed 450 forints to close at 20,050.
New (1997) crop price rises were mainly triggered by speculative buying by one brokerage, a trader said.
Traders added it was uncertain if news about Serb and Croatian interest in Hungarian grain will materialise into real purchases.

They added that BCE futures prices and physical market prices, which stand substantially higher, were becoming closer after a slump on the BCE as Hungary accumulated large stocks of 1996 wheat for which there were no buyers.
However, futures prices were seen going down again later this year on the pressure of excess wheat and maize stocks which will amount to hundreds of thousand tonnes, according to estimates.
"We will sooner or later drown in stocks, and prices will tumble again," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
Maize futures, which usually move in the same direction as wheat, firmed by 150 to 340 forints. Most active May rose 150 and its settlement price was 17,550 forints.
